sourceInformation.source: Advanced Dungeons & Dragons: Treasure of Tarmin (1983)
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge 0.89.1 (8ecc2f6), World3D, Three.js 0.182.0, Rapier 0.19.3, AI Hub session client 1.4.0 (35a1047), JavaScript; all dependencies bundled; Bun 1.3.14 build tool
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural pixel-textured stone, outlined volumetric puppets, warm lanterns and blue runes
sourceInformation.animation: Native Humanoid, Blob, Combo and World3D overlay animation, driven by authoritative events
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-synthesized dungeon and combat music, effects and gibberish voice; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 player shared-world co-op; direct WebRTC offer/answer codes and AI Hub Session Protocol v1; no TURN relay or host migration
sourceInformation.testing: Headless rules/content/authority tests; complete normal-rules solo replay; exact file:// HTML with WebGL2 and WebGPU; Chromium/WebKit/unsupported Firefox; emulated standard controller and phone; Web Audio analysis; real two-browser WebRTC and official Hub standard/stress/host-leave/server/solo scenarios. Real hardware, iOS Safari, cross-network NAT reachability and human listening are unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Scanned Mattel manual, official manual transcript, publisher history and gameplay screenshot inspected; full video playback and original timbres unknown

testingFeedback: 36 distinct issues found and fixed through automated testing and integration review; test-fixture mistakes are excluded. See docs/issues.md.
1 critical/game-breaking issue found and fixed: committing from keyboard/controller during a boss preparation beat recursed instead of continuing the phase. Zero known critical issues remain.

The full normal-rules browser replay, including real Enter/R2 boss-phase transitions: 134 production actions, 61 steps, 27 rounds, all three floors, gate, secret, every boss phase, and separate treasure claim.
Syntax-only checks were least informative: they caught neither gameplay-state errors nor UI/transport lifecycle defects.
engineFeedback: Native World3D turns the same procedural rigs and shape data into a coherent first-person dungeon.
The native camera axes, first-person overlay scale, and Three.js r182 evaluation on browsers without GPUShaderStage required source inspection and integration fixes.
The deterministic dual-strength authority, authored campaign, inventory transactions and network lifecycle.
Bundling the complete 3D dependency graph and reconciling native frame time with host-owned combat deadlines.
Engine and dependency sources are unchanged. The packaging wrapper supplies numeric GPUShaderStage constants when absent so WebGL fallback or a helpful unsupported-renderer screen can start.
Offer a supported single-HTML World3D exporter and shared-world authority example.
promptFeedback: A clear strategic identity, concrete campaign milestones, and explicit verification expectations.
The plan gives suggested folder names while TASK.md owns the exact delivery naming; TASK.md was followed.
Completing simulation, original 3D presentation, controller-first UI and two distinct multiplayer lifecycles together.
Include a small pinned single-file engine/Hub integration starter to leave more effort for authored content.

aiHub.name: Treasure of Tarmin After Dark
aiHub.tagline: Two strengths. Three floors. One way down.
aiHub.description: Carry steel and spirit through three lantern-lit dungeon floors. Read enemy intentions, choose your six-slot burden, defeat the Horned Warden, and claim the treasure alone or with a partner.
aiHub.source: Advanced Dungeons & Dragons: Treasure of Tarmin (1983)
aiHub.controls: WASD/left stick move; Q E/shoulders turn; F/Cross interact; Enter/R2 commit; Tab/Triangle pack; M/touchpad map; X/Square swap; Escape/Options pause.
